title: LAFP: Preserving Latent Action Structure in Latent Policy Learning via Flow Matching
claim: A staged training pipeline replaces collapsing behavior-cloning distillation with flow matching, preserving the multimodal structure of the pretrained latent space.
layout: 6 panels in 2 rows, left-to-right; gray baseline row above green ours row
description: The figure shows a three-stage training pipeline in two rows. A tall left panel, Stage 1 pre-training, is shared by both rows. It has an IDM that takes o_t and o_{t+1} and outputs a latent action z_t, plus an FDM and an action decoder. Inside it, a scatter plot labeled 'unified latent action space' shows clean, color-separated clusters. The top row is grayed out and shows the behavior-cloning baseline. Its Stage 2 distillation plot is a muddled mix of colors, and its Stage 3 post-training uses a fire icon. The bottom row is highlighted in green and shows the proposed flow-matching version. Stage 2 uses a Latent Flow Policy with an interpolation formula and inputs o_t, τ and z_{t,τ}. Its output plot keeps distinct clusters. In Stage 3 the flow policy is frozen (snowflake icon) and feeds the action decoder. Blue, yellow, green, purple and pink boxes mark the different module types. The eye goes first to the contrast between the messy and clean scatter plots.
caption: Overview of LAFP. Stage 1 learns an IDM-induced latent action space with an auxiliary action decoder. Stage 2 distills the frozen IDM targets using conditional flow matching. Stage 3 freezes the flow policy and trains the Post-AD with decoder aligned interpolation to reduce the mismatch between stochastic latent samples and physical action labels.
abstract: Learning high quality latent actions from large-scale unlabeled videos, coupled with limited real-world interaction data for training an action decoder, has emerged as a promising paradigm for scalable latent policy learning. However, existing approaches typically rely on behavior cloning, which tends to collapse inherently multimodal action distributions into unimodal ones, thereby degrading the pretrained latent action structure. While flow matching provides a potential alternative, directly applying it leads to a misalignment between latent actions and physical actions during action decoder training, due to the stochastic nature of the learned policy. To address these, we propose Latent Action Flow Policy (LAFP), which leverages flow matching for latent policy learning and introduces an inference-time interpolation mechanism to mitigate stochasticity-induced misalignment. Experimental results demonstrate that LAFP consistently outperforms prior methods on most downstream imitation learning tasks, achieving an 8.2\% improvement in average success rate while incurring less than 1x additional inference overhead.
